correctness.rationale: For \(0<\lambda<2\), each factor has an exact norm-decrease identity and the positive-definite sum of projectors makes the full linear sweep a strict contraction. Expanding the ordered product and affine term through second order gives the stated analytic fixed-point branch. The residual identities \(\sum_i r_i=0\) and \(P_ir_i=r_i\) make the forward and reverse coefficients cancel exactly. Direct expansion of the scalar three-block example gives a nonzero quadratic midpoint error, proving sharpness.

final_claim: For finite-dimensional cyclic relaxed orthogonal projections with \(S=\sum_iP_i\succ0\), the cyclic fixed point has \(z_\pi(\lambda)=x_*+\lambda h_\pi+O(\lambda^2)\), where \(h_\pi=S^{-1}\sum_{p<q}P_{\pi_q}r_{\pi_p}\); reversing the order gives \(h_{\pi^R}=-h_\pi\), so the midpoint of the two opposite cyclic fixed points is \(x_*+O(\lambda^2)\), and this order is sharp.
